name: Ji Ni Tai Mei (鸡你太美)
blurb: A misheard lyric from a 2017 idol-show video that became a huge 2019 remix meme
title: Ji Ni Tai Mei (鸡你太美) Meme: Meaning, Origin & Trend
description: 鸡你太美 is a misheard lyric of 只因你太美 ("only because you're so beautiful") from Cai Xukun's 2017 Idol Producer intro video. It became a remix meme in January 2019.
h1: What is the Ji Ni Tai Mei (鸡你太美) meme?
answer: 鸡你太美 (jī nǐ tài měi) is a misheard version of the lyric 只因你太美 (zhǐ yīn nǐ tài měi, "only because you're so beautiful"), from a song the singer Cai Xukun performed in his self-introduction video for the talent show Idol Producer, recorded in late 2017. The clip, which mixes dribbling a basketball with dance moves, resurfaced in January 2019 after the NBA named him a Lunar New Year ambassador, and Bilibili users turned it into a flood of remixes (鬼畜). It has stayed one of the most remixed Chinese memes, and also one of the most criticised.

body: The source is a short performance video: the trainee, in a casual outfit, shows basketball moves to iKON's "B-DAY" and then dances to the song 只因你太美 by SWIN-S. Sung quickly, the first syllable 只 (zhǐ) sounds like 鸡 (jī, chicken), so the line was heard as "chicken, you're too beautiful".

That mishearing, plus the unusual mix of basketball and choreography, became raw material for audio-visual remixes. Over time 只因 (zhǐ yīn) itself turned into a joking way to write "chicken", and the dribble-and-dance moves were reused in countless edits.

head: Date
Event
rows: Cai Xukun records his Idol Producer self-introduction video with basketball moves and a dance to 只因你太美
The NBA announces him as its first Lunar New Year ambassador on Weibo; some basketball fans object and the old clip resurfaces
Bilibili creators make large numbers of 鬼畜 remixes around the misheard line 鸡你太美
His side sends a lawyer's letter to Bilibili's operator about remix videos it considers defamatory; "lawyer's letter" jokes join the meme
A Kuaishou creator's video sets off a new wave of remixes, and 只因 spreads as a meme word
A People's Daily Online commentary calls 鸡你太美 and similar phrases vulgar memes that should not reach children

ul: Remix videos that cut the dribble-and-dance clip into music, games or other videos
只因 as a playful word for chicken (鸡), as in "I had 只因 for lunch"
Short codes such as jntm in comments and bullet chats
Recreating the moves in games and animations

body.note: Much of the remixing was aimed at mocking a real person, and the meme has been criticised for spilling into harassment of the performer and his fans. Many people now use it simply as a nostalgic in-joke.

body: The meme peaked in 2019 and again around 2022–2023, and is now a well-known classic of Chinese remix culture. After the 2023 commentary, several trademarks using the phrase were ruled invalid. In 2025 the performer said in an interview with a Bilibili creator that he was thinking of opening an account there, which was widely read as a thaw.

faq.q: What does 鸡你太美 mean?
faq.a: It means nothing on its own: it is a mishearing of 只因你太美 ("only because you're so beautiful"), a lyric in the source video.
只因你太美, a song by SWIN-S, performed in Cai Xukun's self-introduction video for the talent show Idol Producer.

faq.q: What does 只因 mean online?
faq.a: It is a jokey way to write 鸡 (chicken), taken from the first two characters of the lyric.
